title: SLO Partnering Playlab — Canvas & Decision Journal
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an experimental cross-functional playlab for negotiating, implementing, and operationalizing SLOs across product, platform, and SRE. Goal: produce a repeatable 8-week sprint pattern (plus rolling experiments) that yields a deployed SLO, linked alerts, a stubbed runbook, and a post-mortem/quality dashboard for a single candidate service.

Scope & constraints:
- Focus on one medium-risk, high-throughput service (candidate: realtime-embed-proxy).
- Deliverables limited to what we can reasonably ship without infra-wide feature work (no new tracing backend; use existing tracing + prefixed logs).
- Measure per-customer token latency and error rate where feasible; fall back to per-route aggregates.

Expected outputs (end of 8 weeks):
- Negotiated SLO spec (SLO target, error/latency buckets, consumer-facing SLA implications).
- SLO dashboard in Console and a 2-week rolling quality view.
- Alerting rules mapped to runbooks and oncall playbook drafts.
- A/B rollout plan for enforcement and gradual annealing.

High-level timeline (8-week sprint pattern)
Week 0 — Kickoff + Discovery (1 week):
- Workshop (2 hrs): product, platform, SRE, infra, solutions eng. Canvas: user journeys, failure modes, consumer pain.
- Data discovery: what telemetry exists, sample traces, cardinality of keys.
- Decision: accept candidate service or pick next. Owner: Sophie.

Week 1 — Baseline & Hypothesis (1 week):
- Compute 90/95/99 latency and error baselines from last 30 days (Aisha + Marco).
- Hypothesize primary risk vectors (cache warmups, kv GC, autoscaler cold start).
- Draft SLO candidates: e.g., "P95 request latency < 250ms" and "availability >= 99.95%" with exact error definitions.

Week 2 — Instrumentation & Dashboards (1 week):
- Add missing metrics/labels (Devon: tracer tags for model-type, route, customer_tier).
- Implement dashboard mock in Console (slo-embed-proxy-draft).
- Smoke test alert generation on synthetic traffic.

Week 3 — Canary Alerting & Runbook Draft (1 week):
- Create alert rules against a canary project and wire to oncall (Priya).
- Draft runbook steps (escalation path, quick mitigations, fallback model variants).

Week 4-5 — Controlled Rollout (2 weeks):
- Enable SLO monitoring for 10% traffic and measure signal fidelity.
- Run failure injection tests (latency injection, instance termination) in staging to validate SLI sensitivity.

Week 6 — Post-Canary Review & Adjust (1 week):
- Triage metrics, adjust thresholds. Decision gate: ready for org-wide advisory?

Week 7 — Documentation & Handoff (1 week):
- Finalize SLO spec, add linked artifacts (Jira tickets, PRs, Confluence pages).
- Handoff checklist to product and SRE stewards.

Week 8 — Debrief & Next-Service Planning (1 week):
- Run a short retro: capture lessons, update playbook template.
- Kick candidate selection for next service.

Roles & RACI (text form):
- Product PM (Aisha Patel) — Accountable for consumer impact, approves SLO targets.
- Service Owner / Engineering Lead (Marco Ruiz) — Responsible for changes to service, rollout.
- Platform Instrumentation (Devon Martinez) — Responsible for telemetry additions and dashboard plumbing.
- SRE Lead (Priya Rao) — Consulted on alerts, paging, runbooks; approves oncall integration.
- Program Owner (Sophie Chen) — Overall coordination, facilitation, decision log keeper.

SLO Negotiation Template (to use in workshops):
- Customer impact statement: "What user-visible symptom are we protecting?"
- SLI definition (metric source, query, aggregation window): e.g. "P95 request latency across production routes where route != /health, computed as service_latency_ms (histogram) using 60s sliding window"
- Error budget window and burn policy: 30-day rolling, auto-notify at 50% burn, mitigate/rollback at 80% sustained.
- Acceptance criteria: dashboard shows 30 days of data and alerts fire on synthetic regression.

Telemetry & Alert Definitions (draft):
- Primary latency SLI: p95_latency_ms per minute (tagged by route), alert if p95 > target for 5 consecutive 5-min windows.
- Error SLI: request_failure_rate (4xx+5xx counting rules) — alerts at 0.1% sustained (configurable).
- Infrastructure signals: sustained GPU utilization > 85% for 30 minutes; autoscaler thrash > 3x spawns/hr.

Runbook integration checklist (minimal viable runbook):
- Link to SLO spec + Console dashboard
- Triage steps: identify service instance, check model-variant fallbacks, examine KV/cache hit rate, observe recent deploys (last 60 min).
- Quick mitigation recipes: scale up pool, toggle model-variant to smaller quantization, enable prefix cache warm start, route 10% traffic to dedicated capacity pool.
- Escalation path with contact matrix and Slack shortlink.

Experiment log (live notes):
- 2026-03-11: Kickoff workshop. Outcome: pick realtime-embed-proxy. Action: Devon to add customer_tier tag by 3/16.
- 2026-03-15: Baseline computed. P95 = 210ms overall; 99 = 560ms; errors ~0.02%. Hypothesis: tail latencies driven by cold KV misses.
- 2026-03-17: Instrumentation PR #452 added tracer tag model_variant. Synthetic test created (JIRA-RI-1342).
- 2026-03-18: Canary alert flapped during synthetic - root cause: alert window too tight. Action: relax to 5m windows and re-evaluate.

Open risks & unknowns:
- Cardinality explosion if we tag by customer_id; may need sampling or tiered SLO approach.
- Console dashboard quota limits for high-card metrics.
- SLA communication: legal needs to review language if this becomes a public-facing SLA.

Decision journal (short form entries):
- 2026-03-11: Service selection approved (Sophie). Rationale: representative load, several paying customers, manageable telemetry.
- 2026-03-17: Keep P95 target at 250ms (Aisha approved). Evidence: baseline + margin for canary tests.
- 2026-03-18: Alert windows increased to reduce noise (Priya).

Acceptance checklist before final handoff:
- [ ] 30 days of baseline data visible in Console
- [ ] Alerts firing reliably against synthetic regressions
- [ ] Runbook stub linked in Console and SRE handbook
- [ ] Product sign-off on user-impact phrasing and public comms
- [ ] Legal review queued if public SLA is intended

Next immediate actions (owner):
- Devon: finish tag rollout and open PR for dashboard panels (due 2026-03-20).
- Marco: schedule controlled failure injection in staging and document scenarios (due 2026-03-24).
- Aisha: prepare customer-impact blurb and comms draft for partner teams (due 2026-03-22).
- Sophie: maintain decision log and sync retro agenda (ongoing).

Notes to keep informal:
- This is intended as a living playlab. We expect to iterate the cadence (4–12 weeks) depending on service complexity.
- Keep meeting artifacts light: 2 slide summary + decision bullets are usually enough for exec stakeholders.
- Where telemetry is expensive, we should prefer stratified sampling and rate-limited labels rather than full-cardinality metrics by default.

Links & references:
- SLO catalog (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/SLO+Catalog
- Instrumentation guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Tracing+Standards
- Current candidate service PRs: JIRA-RI-1342, JIRA-RI-1391

If you want to run a pilot for a second service at the same time, propose it as a 4-week parallel micro-play: baseline + smoke alerts + canary; keep full runbook for the primary service only.

— Sophie (program owner)
